ai_show_review.summary: Scorching West L.A. Fadeaway debut, fiery Other One, tight jams throughout
ai_show_review.blurb: The Oregon County Fair show bursts with high‑energy playing and several first‑time performances, highlighted by the debut of West L.A. Fadeaway and a monster The Other One → Truckin' sequence. Jerry’s searing leads on Black Peter and powerful vocals on Fadeaway sit atop Brent’s hot keyboards and a thunderous rhythm section. Excellent soundboard recordings capture every nuance.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at the Oregon County Fair is a blistering snapshot of the Dead in full stride during the summer of ’82. The first set rolls through familiar terrain—Bertha, New Minglewood Blues, Tennessee Jed—and then lifts with Althea and the classic China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue. Set two kicks off with the debut of West L.A. Fadeaway, where Jerry’s vocal is as striking as his guitar work and Brent layers funky organ textures that set the tone for a night of soaring improvisation. After a brief dip with Far From Me, the band launches into an expansive Playing In The Band → Drums → Space, emerging into a breathtaking Wheel → The Other One → Truckin' suite that showcases Phil’s vibrating bass, Mickey and Bill’s propulsive drumming, and a black‑sabbath‑level organ on The Other One. The second half caps with a scorching Black Peter and a joyous one‑more‑Saturday‑night finale, all captured in crystal‑clear soundboard mixes that let every nuance shine. For anyone wanting the definitive 1982 outdoor experience—complete with debut material, ferocious jams, and an electrified crowd—the Oregon County Fair recording is essential listening.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with clear instrument separation, no drop‑outs, and the best capture of the West L.A. Fadeaway debut and the high‑energy jams

key_highlights: Debut of West L.A. Fadeaway with hot Brent keyboards and Jerry’s standout vocals
Monster The Other One → Truckin' sequence that rides a thunderous rhythm section
Seared Black Peter featuring scorching guitar leads and tight band interplay
Overall high‑energy outdoor vibe captured in pristine soundboard quality

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers searing leads on Black Peter, powerful vocal on West L.A. Fadeaway, and consistently high‑energy guitar throughout the night.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a blurring, vibrating bass that drives the jams; his low‑end presence is especially felt during The Other One and Truckin'.
band_performance.Bob: Offers intense, fiery vocals and solid rhythm guitar work, anchoring the band through both sets.
band_performance.Brent: Hot keyboards—funky organ on Fadeaway, out‑of‑this‑world swells on The Other One, and vocal contributions that add texture to the performance.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are on fire with a powerful bottom end, fueling the high‑energy flow of both sets.
band_performance.Billy: Locks in with Mickey for a propulsive dual‑drum groove that underpins the extended improvisations.
